newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hanson eyes sale of stake in RGC.
newsitem.headline: Hanson eyes sale of stake in RGC.

text.p: London-based building materials group Hanson Plc has confirmed it will eventually put its 40 percent stake in Australian miner RGC Ltd up for sale.

Hanson deputy chairman Chris Collins said in London on Thursday: "Our stake in RGC is not long term ... But now is not the time to sell." RGC shares were trading at A$3.75 in late trading on Friday, valuing the stake at about A$315 million.
Hanson has in part pinned exceptional charges for the financial half-year to June 30 on writedowns in stake in RGC and its investment in its RGC subisidiary Goldfields Ltd.

There have long been rumours that Hanson would sell out of RGC, which is involved in minerals sand and base metals mining as well as gold through its 57 percent-owned Goldfields. "That's got to be the world's worst kept secret," said one analyst.

Hanson, which has said it is moving out of non-performing assets, attempted to unload RGC last year to insitutions but it failed to achieve its price and retained the stake, sources close to the company said.
"They may have gotten a little greedy and wanted a bit more than the institutions wanted to pay," one said.
Hanson on Thursday announced a first-half pre-tax profit of 47.8 million stg after taking a sting for over 49 million pounds in charges.
Since the last attempts to sell the stake, the market outlook for mineral sands has dimmed, suggesting Hanson may have missed its chance to sell at the top of the market, one analyst said.
In gold, Goldfields is facing high mining costs at its Paddington mine and declining reserves at its Henty deposit.
Goldfields was formed about two years ago through the joining of RGC's gold assets and those of Pancontinental Mining Ltd.
Despite efforts to create a succesfull "pure gold play," Goldfields has returned dissapointing results for investors.
The Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea is considered one of the strongest assets, analysts said.
Goldfields' net profits fell to A$3.56 million in the half-year to December 31 from A$4.31 a year earlier.
"If it wasn't for hedging, Paddington would be a very marginal mine," an analyst in Sydney said.
RGC in June said it expected its 1996/97 net profit be less than half the A$76.5 million achieved in the previous year.
Expectations of lower profits were linked to a A$50 million writedown of RGC's Thalanga base metals mine in Queensland and a A$30 million writedown of its Renison tin mine in Tasmania.
